messages:
Alex: Quick sync — proposing a canonical metric set for Hosted + Dedicated GPU pools. Need buy-in from runtime, infra, console, and SRE. TL;DR: SM occupancy %, GPU memory (alloc vs resident), queue depth (ready requests), and a per-pool headroom metric. Thoughts?

Mira: +1. Can we define sampling & retention upfront? occupancy is noisy. Propose 10s sampling for raw sm_occupancy, 1m for queue_depth, 30s for memory. Raw ingest 7d, aggregated hourly 90d.

Jordan: storage cost caveat — agree on cadence but want low-cardinality exports. Do we intend per-GPU, per-pool, per-model, per-tenant? cardinality explodes.

Leila: For visibility we need per-pool + per-model rollups. Per-tenant should be opt-in (privacy/contract reasons). Default API should only expose pool/model aggregates; tenant-level only with ACL and opt-in.

Sam: Quick defs so dashboards/alerts are consistent: how do we compute SM occupancy percent?

Alex: Suggested formula: occupancy = (active_compute_warps / total_warps) * 100 averaged over window. Practically: count active wavefronts per SM over 10s then normalize by SM_count * warp_slots. Example metric names:

``` 
sm_occupancy_percent{pool="hosted-prod",gpu_id="g0"} = 78.3
gpu_memory_bytes_used{pool="dedicated-c123",gpu_id="g1"} = 12345678912
queue_depth{pool="hosted-prod",route="/v1/generate"} = 23
headroom_score{pool="dedicated-c123"} = 0.42  # 0..1 where 1 is full headroom
```

Mira: Nice. For headroom calc we should combine occupancy, memory pressure (resident/total), and scheduling queue depth. Propose normalized score for UI color-coding.

Casey: Dashboard UX request: Console should show a compact heatmap across pools and a per-pool detail page with timeseries + top contributors (models/routes). Also a canary widget that can surface the same metrics for canary rollouts.

Jordan: On instrumentation ownership: runtime team should emit sm_occupancy and queue_depth at per-GPU granularity. Infra should enrich with topology (rack, region), GPU type, and handle memory resident accounting. Telemetry pipeline will then roll up.

Leila: Agree. Also need a clear contract: metric name, type (gauge/counter), tags, unit, and semantic meaning. Who writes the metrics proto? runtime owns proto and initial schema; infra owns mapping/enrichment and the rollup pipeline config.

Sam: Alerting thresholds idea: occupancy > 85% for 3m -> non-urgent page, occupancy > 95% for 30s -> urgent, queue_depth > X for 5m -> paging. Need SRE to set X per-pool.

Alex: Also want routing policy hooks: e.g., if pool headroom_score < 0.2, route-new-requests -> fallback model variant or redirect to Dedicated pools. That implies the routing service needs an API from telemetry: current pool headroom + recent trend. Should be low-latency (sub-30s).

Mira: For low-latency signals we should publish a small set of "fast metrics" (headroom_score, occupancy_short_window) via a streaming channel (kafka/pubsub) besides timeseries. Avoid querying long-term TSDB for routing decisions.

Jordan: Streaming sounds right. Telemetry team: ensure ordering and backpressure so routing service isn't impacted. Also add sequence numbers to fast signals.

Leila: ACLs again — streaming endpoints must enforce customer-level boundaries. Dedicated pools expose tenant tags; Hosted should mask tenant ids unless allowed.

Casey: Console integration: canary rollout screen should show the fast metrics + p95 latency + queue_depth. Minimal UI: sparkline + current value + trend arrow + small heatmap for pooled GPUs.

Sam: Metric naming suggestions (to standardize across teams):
- sm_occupancy_percent (gauge)
- queue_depth_pending (gauge)
- gpu_memory_bytes_used (gauge)
- gpu_memory_bytes_reserved (gauge)
- headroom_score (gauge 0..1)

Alex: Agree. Also add metadata tag: sampling_window="10s" or "1m" to help consumers.

Mira: Retention again: raw 10s samples -> 7d, 1m aggregates -> 30d, hourly aggregates -> 365d. Is that too long for cost?

Jordan: That 365d hourly seems OK for trend analysis but let's gate it behind a storage estimate. We'll do a quick cost calc once schema finalized.

Leila: Who will own dashboards? product/console will ship the UI but we need dashboard templates in grafana for SRE and runtime. Recommend runtime owns templates and infra owns the rendered provisioning in grafana/console.

Alex: Action items:
- runtime: draft metrics proto + example emitter for sm_occupancy/queue_depth (due EOD Fri)
- infra/telemetry: design rollup config + streaming fast-signal API (due next Wed)
- console/product: mockups for pool heatmap, per-pool page, canary widget (due next Tue)
- SRE: propose alert thresholds per-pool (initial draft next Wed)

Jordan: I'll take telemetry rollup config with infra.

Mira: I'll own sampling/retention document and coordinate cost estimate with finance.

Leila: Runtime will send a proto PR by Fri.

Sam: SRE will draft thresholds and add a simple pagerplaybook.

Casey: UI mockups incoming Tuesday. I'll also add a small user story for canary UX.

infra-bot: noted. linked runbook: https://redwood.example/runbooks/gpu-capacity

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for hosted-prod small-signal test. monitor: sm_occupancy_percent, queue_depth_pending, p95_latency.

Alex: Great sync. If no objections I'll schedule a cross-team follow-up (30m) next Thu. :thumbsup:
